Migrates the **HP 11713A Attenuator/Switch Driver** (#6) from the HP-Attenuator reference into the new `GpibUtils.Instruments.Switches` project, onto the shared vendor-neutral transport, and adds its `gpibutils hp11713a` CLI branch (#45).

## What landed
- **`Hp11713ACommandBuilder`** — dB → A/B relay-string solver (fewest sections), switch/validation helpers.
- **`AttenuatorConfig`** — configurable wiring; default 8494 (0-11 dB) + 8496 (0-110 dB) = **0-121 dB in 1 dB steps**.
- **`Hp11713A`** — driver over `IInstrumentSession`; independent S9/S0 switches; software state shadow (11713A is listen-only); configurable address (default `GPIB0::28::INSTR`); `--invert-sense`.
- **`Hp11713ASimulatedDevice`** — decodes A/B data strings back into relay state, so the driver is verifiable with **no hardware**.
- **CLI (#45):** `hp11713a set | engage | zero | switch9 | switch0 | raw`, with `--provider` / `--address` / `--timeout` / `--config` / `--invert-sense` at the leaf and self-documenting `--help` at every level.
- **Foundation:** `SimulatedInstrument.WriteObserver` hook so simulated listen-only instruments can track state driven purely by writes.

## Verification (no hardware)
- **46 unit tests green** (25 new): command-builder math, full-range reachability, sense inversion, switches, and end-to-end driver→Simulated-session→decoded-relay-state.
- CLI exercised live against the Simulated provider (`set`/`engage`/`switch`/`--config swapped`/out-of-range/invalid-raw).

## Not done here — needs the bench
Per the [no-hardware policy](docs/HARDWARE_VERIFICATION.md), this merges simulator-green. **Issue #6 stays open in 🟡 Verification Needed** (tag `verify/6-hp11713a`) until the A/B relay strings are confirmed against a real 11713A + 8494/8496 attenuators. Tracked on #46.

body:
The Email view pill opened a bare new tab. Now it toggles like the TUI view: the article swaps for a **mail-client window in-page** — the paper as a received message.

## What it looks like

- **Window chrome**: traffic lights + "Barkpark Mail · Inbox (1)" — the unread count and subject dot settle once the message has been "read" (a beat after open).
- **Toolbar**: back / archive / trash all *file the mail away* — they return you to the reader. The star is a local nicety.
- **Sender header**: BP avatar, **Barkpark Papers** `<papers@barkpark.cloud>`, "to me ▾", received stamp formatted like an inbox ("tor. 9. juli, 04:33 (just now)").
- **Message body**: an `<iframe>` of the LITERAL `/papers/:slug/email` response — the exact bytes a mail backend sends (Render.render_document, all inline). No CSS imitation; the same honesty rule as the TUI view. Lazy `src` on first activation, same-origin height auto-fit.
- **Footer**: Reply / Forward are real `mailto:` links; "View in browser ↗" keeps the raw-bytes tab.
- **Theme-aware chrome**: a dark mail client showing the light HTML email, exactly like real clients — the message bytes never change with the theme.

## Mechanics

- Three-way view state `reader | tui | email` in the existing `bp-paper-view` localStorage key; modes mutually exclusive; inside an alternate view only that view's own pill shows, as the way back.
- Layout-only change in `bulldocs.html.heex` — render pipeline untouched. Script stays at the end of `<body>` (golden rule 4).

## Verification

- `mix test` on the layout gates: reader_dark_token_parity + stylesheet + render_sheet — 43 tests, 0 failures (the new `--mail-*` dark tokens only ADD to reader dark coverage).
- Static harness (layout chrome + live guerrilla email bytes) + headless Chrome, light AND dark: mode/class switching, article hidden, subject + date + mailto wiring, iframe auto-fit (8361px on the showcase), persistence + restore round-trip, `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out.

author: hoyalim
body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the exec approval path and understand the authorization boundary changed by this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer pays for a fresh reviewer completion whenever the same ask-requiring gateway request is reviewed again. Retry and polling loops can therefore turn N identical reviews into N paid model calls even though the reviewer runs deterministically at temperature 0.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a bounded per-reviewer-instance memo with deliberately narrow reuse semantics:

- cache only completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions for `host=gateway`;
- require a non-empty canonical gateway `resolvedPath` before caching;
- key command, argv, resolved executable, cwd, environment keys, reason, analysis, and agent context;
- never cache node-host requests, `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, completion-error, or other fallback outcomes;
- cap the memo at 128 entries.

Node-host reuse was explicitly removed after review because its current prepare protocol does not expose a separate canonical resolved-executable field to the reviewer. This avoids crossing node or executable authorization boundaries rather than widening the protocol in a cost-optimization PR.

## User Impact

For N byte-identical gateway requests within one reviewer instance, paid reviewer completions drop from N to 1. Changed resolved executables trigger a fresh completion, and node requests retain the existing per-call review behavior.

## Evidence

Final rebase:

- `upstream/main`: `2e6fd00871b`
- branch head: `bb95ca4b779`

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` -> 86/86 tests passed on the final rebased head.
- `oxfmt --check` on both changed files -> passed.
- LOC ratchet and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` -> passed.
- The full changed-file gate passed on the prior broader code tree, including core typecheck, core-test typecheck (822.82s), lint, LOC, format, dependency, import-cycle, database-first, and security guards. The final patch removes the node-host/protocol changes that tree contained and reruns the focused tests above.

Configured provider-backed runtime proof used OpenClaw's production config validation, model/auth resolution, reviewer, and OpenAI-compatible streaming HTTP transport against a local deterministic endpoint:

| Gateway request | Cumulative real completion POSTs |
| --- | ---: |
| baseline | 1 |
| byte-identical repeat | 1 |
| changed `resolvedPath` | 2 |

Both real completion calls were `POST /v1/chat/completions` with configured bearer auth, `model=reviewer-proof`, `stream=true`, and `temperature=0`; each returned a parsed low-risk `allow-once` decision. Script SHA-256: `516b27f2f7a43cac44924104306d243796be0cc87ac91494ac207f408d9a0c2b`.

Focused invariants also prove duplicate `ask` and node-host inputs are never memoized.

## Why

Two teammates hitting the same wall: `mvn spring-boot:run` dies with `java.net.NoRouteToHostException: No route to host`. It looks like a bad password, and the README's troubleshooting put the password bullet right above the network one — so the tempting fix is resetting the shared database password, which breaks everyone else's `.env`.

The actual cause is that `db.<ref>.supabase.co` **has no IPv4 address**:

```
$ dig +short db.sbjisgesmhxktwtjohlt.supabase.co A      # (empty)
$ dig +short db.sbjisgesmhxktwtjohlt.supabase.co AAAA
2600:1f16:c40:6e00:32ce:bfaa:3157:f34

author: wolffruoff
body:
## Problem

Every scrape started failing at `browser.new_context()`:

```
playwright._impl._errors.Error: Browser.new_context: Protocol error
(Browser.setDefaultViewport): ... Found property "<root>.viewport.isMobile"
- false which is not described in this scheme
```

This is **dependency drift**, not a code bug:

- The Dockerfile installs from `pyproject.toml` (`pip install .`) and **ignores `uv.lock`**.
- `pyproject.toml` had `camoufox[geoip]>=0.4`, and `camoufox 0.4.11` declares `playwright` with **no version bound**.
- So an image rebuild resolved **playwright 1.61.0** (latest). Camoufox 0.4.11 ships a fixed patched-Firefox build (146.0.1) whose CDP protocol doesn't accept the `viewport.isMobile` field that playwright 1.61 sends → `new_context()` fails before any page loads.

Known-good pairing (local venv + `uv.lock`): **playwright 1.58.0 + camoufox 0.4.11**.

## Fix

Pin the browser-coupled deps in `pyproject.toml` to the lockfile-matching pair so `pip install .` can't drift:

```
camoufox[geoip]==0.4.11
playwright==1.58.0
```

`uv lock` regenerated (no version changes — both were already 1.58.0 / 0.4.11).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The deeper issue is that the Docker build doesn't honor `uv.lock`. Switching the Dockerfile to `uv sync --frozen` would make the whole dependency set reproducible and prevent future drift on any package. Happy to do that separately if you want it.

## Testing
- Full scraper suite: **187 passed**.
- Rebuild the image and confirm `new_context()` succeeds / USPS scrapes return data.

## What & why

Platform admins can now **transfer a firm's owner** to another active member of the same firm, from the admin enterprise detail page (`/admin/enterprises/[id]`). This pairs with the existing "change subdomain" admin control.

Ownership stays **inside the firm** — the new owner must already be an active member, which guarantees they have an `AdvisorProfile` (needed to re-point the tenant subdomain).

## How the transfer works

New **"Firm owner"** card shows the current owner and a picker of the firm's other active members. On confirm, `changeEnterpriseOwnerByAdmin` runs one atomic transaction:

1. Demote the current owner → **ADMIN** (keeps firm-wide access; owner is determined by membership role, and ADMIN already grants firm-wide access)
2. Promote the chosen member → **OWNER**
3. Re-point the tenant subdomain's `advisorId` to the new owner's profile
4. Move the firm's `billingContactUserId` to the new owner

After commit: bust the proxy subdomain cache, write an `ENTERPRISE_OWNER_CHANGE` audit row, and notify both the new owner and the demoted previous owner (best-effort).

**Stripe customer / subscription stay enterprise-scoped and are untouched.**

## Guardrails

- New owner must be an **active member of this firm** with an advisor profile
- Can't pick the current owner
- Blocks the transfer if the new owner already holds a **different** portal subdomain (would collide on the unique `advisorSubdomain.advisorId`)

author: chiyanram
body:
Closes #83.

`dot update` misreported the Homebrew step two ways, both from fragile log greps
in `update_homebrew`:

- **False failure**: `grep -q "Error\|fatal\|Failed" "$RUN_LOG"` marked the step
  failed whenever brew's chatty output contained those substrings (cask caveats,
  non-fatal warnings) — even after a clean 11-package upgrade.
- **False "changed"**: `grep -q "=>"` matched brew's always-present
  `==> Updating Homebrew...` header, so the step reported "changed" on every run,
  including `Already up-to-date`.

## Fix (test-first, mirrors #81)

Extract a pure `_brew_update_outcome <exit_status> <log> → failed|changed|ok`:
- **failure = the exit code alone** (brew returns non-zero on a real failure;
  its output text must never flip a success).
- **changed = a real upgrade marker** (`==> Upgrad(ing|ed)` or a
  `name old -> new` line), not a bare `=>`.

`tests/update_homebrew.bats` covers both real success messages and the two
false-positive cases (up-to-date → ok; benign "Failed" text + exit 0 → not
failed). The two bug cases were verified red against the old logic, then green
after the fix. `./bin/dot-test` passes.

## 배경 (이슈 #3)
결제토큰 생성 → 데드볼트 열림까지 정상 진행 후:
1. Edge_Environment health check에 `door_state: 'error'` 지속 (`queue_pending: 0`, `barrier_satisfied: true`)
2. crk-model-hg가 trigger 처리·판단 로그를 전혀 출력하지 않음 (uvicorn access log만)

## 원인 — 원본 CRK-model 대비 이관에서 생략된 3가지

### 1. 세션 ID가 고정 `"global"` (원본: OPEN마다 `global_session_id` 발급)
`EventLog`는 확정된 세션의 이벤트를 영구 거부(I11)하고 settler 멱등 캐시도 session_id 키. ID가 고정이면 **첫 세션 확정 후 모든 트리거가 rejected → 모든 세션이 첫 결과(또는 blocked→ERROR)를 반복**. door_state가 error로 고착되는 메커니즘.

### 2. barrier_timeout이 처리 중(in-flight) 트리거에도 발화 (원본: pending trigger 대기)
Jetson AVI 디코드+TensorRT 추론이 close_timeout(10s)보다 길면 `queue_pending` 상태에서 ERROR. 이후 워커가 완료 → 이슈 health의 `queue_pending: 0 / barrier_satisfied: true / door_state: error`와 정확히 일치. 원본 `handle_close_signal`은 pending trigger가 있는 한 finalize하지 않고 대기.

### 3. 도메인 로깅 전무 (원본: `[TRIGGER]`/`[MULTI-ZONE]`/`[SUMMARY]` 상세 로깅)
HG 전체에 로깅 0줄 + `serve.py`에 logging 설정 없음 (uvicorn `log_level`은 uvicorn 로거만 다룸) — 로그가 전혀 안 보인 직접 원인.

## 수정
- **`model_service`**: OPEN 시 gateway가 IDLE/FINALIZED/ERROR면 새 세션 ID 발급(`ses-N-<epoch>`), ACTIVE/PENDING_CLOSE면 유지 → 세션 격리 + **ERROR에서 다음 OPEN으로 자동 복구**
- **`state_machine`**: `queue_pending`(처리 중)은 close_timeout 대신 별도 stall 상한(기본 120s, `MODEL__CLOSE__WORKER_STALL_TIMEOUT_S`) 적용, 트리거 처리 완료 시 진행으로 간주해 리셋 — 워커 사망 fail-closed(I17/D9)는 유지
- **로깅 복원**: 트리거 수신/처리 결과(판정·delta·YOLO 호출 수·사유 코드·처리 시간), OPEN/CLOSE 전이, FINALIZED 정산 요약, ERROR 사유(blocked/timeout) + `serve.py` basicConfig + 워커 스레드 예외 방어

## 검증
- 전체 **87 passed** (회귀 테스트 3개 추가: 연속 세션 독립 정산, ERROR→OPEN 복구, 추론 지연 중 close_timeout 생존)
- 이슈 시나리오 E2E 재현: 세션1 error → **세션2 OPEN 시 door_state `active` 복구** → CLOSE+30s 추론 중 `processing` 유지 → 완료 시 `complete`(1500원), 전 단계 로그 출력 확인

## Summary

Adds `Get-SasLogPerformance_v1.ps1`, a PowerShell 5.1–compatible, Task Scheduler–ready crawler that parses SAS 9.4 logs into a per-step performance inventory (one row per PROC / DATA step / initialization / session total), plus sample config CSVs and synthetic SAS 9.4 sample logs used to validate the parser.

### Script highlights
- **Inputs**: root directories from `input_directories.csv` (`FULL_PATH_DIR`), with `-LogRoot` fallback (defaults to the UNIT logs UNC path); folder exclusions via `folder_exclusion_list.csv` (case-insensitive, trailing-slash-safe); extensions filter defaults to `log`,`txt`,`sas`.
- **Parser**: recognizes `NOTE: PROCEDURE <NAME> used`, `NOTE: DATA statement used`, `NOTE: SAS initialization used:`, `NOTE: The SAS System used:`; normalizes `ss.ff`, `mm:ss.ff`, and `h:mm:ss.ff` to decimal seconds (raw strings kept); captures user/system CPU, memory, OS Memory, Step/Switch counts, log open/close timestamps, and ERROR/WARNING counts. Reads with Windows-1252 so `©` bytes never crash a run. Stub logs emit exactly one `NO_STEPS_FOUND` row; unreadable files emit a `PARSE_ERROR` row and the run continues.
- **Program name derivation**: schedule-suffix regex (`_\d{3,5}(AM|PM)$`), then version-suffix regex (`_V\d+(_\d+)*$`), then optional Strip-Tokens-style literal tokens, then trailing `_`/`.` trim, with `SAS_PROGRAM_NAME_SOURCE` = `SUFFIX_TRIMMED` / `FILENAME_UNTRIMMED`.
- **Output**: extension-driven — `.csv` via `Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation`; `.xlsx` via ImportExcel module → Excel COM → graceful CSV fallback with warning. Sheet name honored via `-ExcelSheetName`.
- **Ops**: `Write-Log` console + rolling file log (`Get-SasLogPerformance.log`, 5 MB roll), optional CSV-driven robocopy staging (args built as an array, exit codes 0–7 = success, no `Invoke-Expression`), SMTP relay completion/failure email, comment-based help (`Get-Help` verified), exit codes 0 / 1 (parse errors) / 2 (fatal).

### Validation performed (PowerShell 7.6 on Linux)
- `DME_Prepay_Top_Denials_V1_1_1200PM.log` → 34 step rows: 20 PROCEDURE SQL, 8 DATA_STEP, 2 IMPORT, 2 PRINT, 1 INITIALIZATION, 1 SESSION_TOTAL; session real time `35:17.06` → **2117.06 s**; user+system CPU summed (165.12 + 15.34 = 180.46).
- Both 2-line stub logs → exactly one `NO_STEPS_FOUND` row each.
- All 7 sample program names trim per spec (`DME_Prepay_Top_Denials`, `DME_7Z_Denial_Monthly_Reporting`, `DME_Probe_Summary_Edit_Effectiveness_Qtly`, `DMEB_POE_Qtrly_Report`, …).
- `.xlsx` rerun honors the `LogMetrics` sheet name (Export-Excel path); with no Excel option available the script falls back to CSV alongside with warnings.
- Broken file → `PARSE_ERROR` row + exit code 1; excluded folder skipped; unreachable roots warn and exit cleanly.

### Notes
- The original `sample_logs/` and `sample_programs/` reference folders were not present in the repository, so `sample_logs/` here contains **synthetic** SAS 9.4 fixtures built to the spec (see `sample_logs/README.md`); the described conventions of the existing utilities (CSV-driven robocopy, `Send-MailMessage` via smtprelay port 25, Strip-Tokens suffix trimming) were followed from the task description.
- Windows-only pieces (Excel COM, `Get-Acl` owner, robocopy, `Send-MailMessage`) are guarded and degrade gracefully; final verification of the ImportExcel/COM paths on a real Windows + Office box is recommended.

## O que foi feito

O enunciado cita explicitamente "Monolito vs Microserviços" como exemplo de decisão difícil a documentar em ADR — e era a única decisão dessa lista que ainda não tinha uma. A pergunta é inevitável na avaliação de um sistema financeiro com docs de escala (1M tx/min), então a resposta merece estar no repositório, não só na cabeça do autor.

## O argumento registrado

- **Fator decisivo**: a liquidação é hoje um único commit ACID no Postgres, atendendo literalmente "nenhuma liquidação pode ficar pela metade". Decompor em serviços transformaria isso em saga com compensação — consistência eventual exatamente onde há dinheiro.
- **Condições para microserviços não existem aqui**: um domínio coeso, um time, um deploy (Lei de Conway ao contrário).
- **Fronteiras internas com disciplina de serviço**: camadas sem violação de dependência, motor de precificação puro — extração futura é mecânica.
- **Caminho de decomposição documentado**: EDA (outbox) + sharding por cedente já desenham a evolução; a ADR registra o **critério de reversão explícito** (múltiplos times, divergência de perfil de carga além do que read replica resolve).

## Observação

Commit pós-tag `v1.0.0` (documentação evolutiva — a tag da entrega permanece intocada no commit original).

body:
## Problem

Encoding a long video runs the Qwen3-VL vision flash-attention kernel over
all `t*h*w` patches in a single call (43008 for a 384x8x14 clip),
overflowing TPU VMEM and killing EngineCore:

```
jax.errors.JaxRuntimeError: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: E1001: CompileTimeScopedVmemOom:
Ran out of memory in memory space vmem while allocating on stack for
%flash_attention.1 = bf16[1,2,43008,72] custom-call(...),
custom_call_target="tpu_custom_call".
Scoped allocation with size 42.25M and limit 32.00M exceeded scoped vmem limit by 10.25M.
```

Origin: vision `_forward_sdpa` -> flash_attention, inside
`_process_video_input` (`self.visual(pixel_values_videos, grid_thw)`).

## Fix

Add an opt-in `MM_ENCODER_FRAME_CHUNK` env knob (0 = off, current
behavior). When set, `execute_mm_encoder` slices a single large video into
temporal chunks of at most N frames, encodes each chunk via the existing
`embed_multimodal_fn`, and concatenates the per-chunk outputs on the token
axis. The concat is done on host then moved back to device with the
chunks' sharding, avoiding a per-shape XLA recompile and holding every
chunk buffer in HBM at once.

Lossless: Qwen3-VL vision attention is segmented per frame (`cu_seqlens`
has one entry per frame; there are no window / full-attention blocks) and
its position embeddings are spatial-only, so a frame never attends across
frame boundaries -- chunking is bit-exact. Deepstack features ride the
hidden axis and are preserved by the token-axis concat. Auto-disables when
EVS video-token pruning (`video_pruning_rate`) is on, since that selects
tokens across the whole video.

Falls back to a single un-chunked call unless: the knob is on, it's a
single video item larger than one chunk, and pruning is off.

author: dev-siegel
body:
## Problem

The mol-dog-doctor order (5m cadence) measures its connectivity probe with whole-second `date +%s` stamps. The duration is therefore floor-quantized: a millisecond-scale probe that straddles an epoch-second boundary measures exactly **1s**, and the `>=` comparison against the 1s default threshold mailed a false `Dolt health advisory [MEDIUM]` on a healthy server — ~10×/day (straddle probability ≈ real probe duration ≈ 4-6% for the observed 40-60ms probe × 288 runs/day), 100+ archived from the mayor inbox since 7/4. Bead: cc-yju7t.

## Fix

Compare **strictly-greater**. Under floor quantization, `measured > threshold` guarantees the real duration exceeded the threshold, while a sub-second probe can never measure above 1s:

- the false-positive class (healthy sub-second probe) is eliminated **deterministically** — no debounce state needed;
- every genuine multi-second degradation still fires (`measured ≥ 2` ⇒ real > 1s);
- the documented 1s threshold semantic and the env override (`GC_DOCTOR_LATENCY_WARN_S`) keep working; warn text updated `>=` → `>` to state what is enforced.

Alternatives considered: threshold bump to 2 (equivalent live behavior but misstates intent as "2s tolerated"); millisecond probes (needs bash≥5 `EPOCHREALTIME` or a python3/perl dependency in a deliberately plain bash+coreutils script — heavier than the problem warrants).

## Tests

- `TestDoctorScriptLatencyBoundaryStraddleDoesNotWarn` — stepping fake `date` (1000→1001) pins the exact straddle; asserts the summary shows the 1s reading (proves the fake clock drove the measurement, no vacuous pass) and **no** advisory mail. Mutation-checked: FAILS against the pre-fix script.
- `TestDoctorScriptGenuineLatencyDegradationStillWarns` — fake date 1000→1003; asserts the advisory fires with the `latency 3s > threshold 1s` text.
- Sender-identity test updated: forces the advisory path with threshold `-1` (was `0`, which relied on `>=`).

Gates: `gofmt` clean, `go vet` clean, `bash -n` clean, full `./examples/dolt` suite green (147s).

## Rollout note

dolt is a REQUIRED pack — this ships to the live city only via a gc binary carrying it (same surgical-binary path as #2/#3; next release must carry 8aa2021 + b1f68852 + this).

author: devinjameson
body:
## What and why

DevTools reconstructs Submodel lineage for history entries by walking the `Got*Message` wrappers on the dispatched Message (`extractSubmodelInfo`). A Command, though, crosses to DevTools as `{ name, args }` only, so at the point you inspect it in the Commands tab (or via the `foldkit_get_message` / `foldkit_get_init` MCP tools) there is no way to say which Submodel its eventual result will land in. That attribution only materializes later, once the resolved result is recorded as its own entry.

Since the message-mapping-chain work (#670), `Command.mapMessage` / `mapMessages` record their lifts on the Command as a recoverable chain. This uses it to pre-attribute a Command to its destination Submodel, up front, without running the Effect. Purely additive: nothing read the chain before, so exposing it can only add attribution.

## What changed

- **Recover the path** (`foldkit`): `toCommandRecord` folds a Command's recorded `messageMappers` chain over a probe leaf and reduces it to a serializable `submodelPath` of `Got*Message` wrapper tags from outer to inner, the same shape entries carry. `CommandRecord`, `toSerializedCommand`, and the `SerializedCommand` wire schema now carry `submodelPath` (empty for a top-level Command). There is no `maybeLeafTag`: the result Message does not exist until the Effect resolves, so the destination is known but the arriving Message is not. `commandSubmodelPath` lives beside `extractSubmodelInfo` and reuses it; `messageMappersOf` is a new internal accessor for the chain.
- **Probe mode** (`foldkit`): a real `Got*Message` wrapper validates its `message` field via `Schema.make` and rejects the structurally-invalid probe. The callable tagged-struct constructors (`m`, `r`, `ts`) gain an internal `withConstructorProbe` mode that stamps the `_tag` without decoding the payload. It is synchronous, restored in a `finally`, and only active during the DevTools fold, which itself only runs when a DevTools store is attached.
- **Surface it** (`@foldkit/devtools`): the Commands tab renders each Command's destination Submodel path as a small label above the Command, mirroring the existing entry submodel-path treatment.
- **Document it** (`@foldkit/devtools-mcp`): the `foldkit_get_message` and `foldkit_get_init` tool descriptions note the new `submodelPath` field on each Command.

## Design decision

The probe is folded through the actual recorded chain rather than reading a tag stored at `mapMessage` time. Storing a tag eagerly would have to probe the user's mapper on the production hot path, and the whole point of the chain is that it stays inert metadata the runtime never reads. Folding under a transient probe mode keeps production dispatch untouched and confines the validation bypass to the DevTools code path. The alternative, catching the validation throw per level, cannot recover the wrapper `_tag` from the error, so it does not work.

## Scope

Deliberately out of scope, and called out as separate in the issue: correlating a parent Command to the specific future child history entry, and Mount submodel attribution. Both can build on this same recovered-path idea later.

## Verification

- New unit tests drive `commandSubmodelPath` with real validating constructors (empty chain, single wrapper, nested wrapper with asserted outer→inner order, and a non-`Got` fold that yields an empty path), proving the probe mode is load-bearing since those constructors throw without it.
- New tests cover `withConstructorProbe` directly: stamp-over-invalid-payload, validation restored after the probe returns, and normal validation outside a probe.
- Serialize and store tests updated to carry `submodelPath`.
- Full local suite green: build, all-package typecheck, lint, dead-code, format, foldkit tests (1509 passed), changeset-unwrapped, commit-message-line-length, no-major-changesets. The pre-push hook (which also runs the website e2e) passed on push.

Changesets: `foldkit` minor, `@foldkit/devtools` minor, `@foldkit/devtools-mcp` patch.

Adds a `.worktreeinclude` at the repo root so Claude Code copies the gitignored local files a fresh per-session worktree needs to run the local gate.

```
.env                  # Django settings: DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY, DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE, Stripe/Telegram keys — required by `make test` and any manage.py command
frontend/.env.local   # NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL — inlined into the static export at build time by `cd frontend && npm run build`
```

Only gitignored files that match a pattern are copied, so tracked files (e.g. the committed `.env.example`) are never duplicated. Rebuildable dirs (`.venv/`, `frontend/node_modules/`, `frontend/out/`) are deliberately **not** listed — they are rebuilt per worktree, not copied.

## Why

Phase 1 of `docs/parallel-work-harness-directive.md` (Layer 1 — isolation). The discipline is that every session works in its own worktree and the primary checkout is an integration station, not a shared work surface. A fresh worktree is a clean checkout with no `.env`, so without this file it cannot run `make test` or the frontend build — which defeats the point of isolating work you can verify in place. `.claude/worktrees/` is already gitignored, so worktrees never show up as untracked noise.

Verified against the current Claude Code worktree docs: `.worktreeinclude` lives at the repo root, uses `.gitignore` syntax, and copies matching gitignored files into worktrees created via `--worktree`, subagent `isolation: worktree`, and desktop parallel sessions.

Do not merge yet — the orchestrator uses this PR in a later deploy-serialization race test.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Fixes CLI-side broken functionality found in stress testing against the v1.4.0 backend. All changes are targeted edits to existing command files; no new command modules and no SDK regeneration.

### `ak lifecycle create` always returned 422
The command sent a `max_severity`/`block_on_fail` body, but the backend's `POST /api/v1/admin/lifecycle` requires `policy_type` + `config` (retention-style policy). The generated SDK models the stale shape, so the request is now built directly. New flags: `--policy-type`, `--config` (JSON), plus optional `--description`/`--priority`/`--repo`/`--cron-schedule`. Policy type and config JSON are validated client-side, and backend validation errors are surfaced with a clean message.

### Mutation verbs ignored `--format json`
Create/update/delete verbs printed a prose sentence to stderr and nothing to stdout, so scripts could not capture created IDs or pipe to `jq`. A shared `emit_mutation` helper now:
- `--format json`/`yaml`: emits the created/updated object (or a structured result) to **stdout**
- `--format quiet`: prints just the id
- default table: keeps the human message on stderr

Applied across repo, group, license, permission, profile, sync-policy, webhook, promotion, admin (user/plugin), sso, scan, quality-gate, sbom, peer, label, lifecycle, and artifact.

### `sign key create` help/default used an unsupported algorithm
`ed25519` is rejected by the backend (only `rsa2048`/`rsa4096`). The default and help example now use `rsa4096`.

### `sso test` always hit the LDAP endpoint
Added `--type`; only LDAP has a backend connectivity-test route, so OIDC/SAML are now rejected with a clear message instead of a confusing 404.

### `repo create` help showed wrong flags
Examples referenced `--type`/`--url`; corrected to the real `--repo-type`/`--upstream-url`.

## Verification

Built `--release`; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings -A dead_code`, and `cargo test --workspace` (1449 passed) all clean. Each fixed command was re-run against the live v1.4.0 backend and confirmed working (JSON captured via `jq`, IDs captured in quiet mode, lifecycle create returns 200). Test objects created during verification were cleaned up.

## Note on the reported "six commands 404" (F3)
On current `main`, `artifact copy`, `sbom get/components/export`, `license check`, `quality-gate check`, and `scan security show` all reach the correct endpoints and return 200 with valid input — verified live. The stress-test 404s were business-precondition responses (no license policy configured / no enabled quality gate) or a repo UUID passed where a key is expected, not path drift. No path changes were needed for those; they are documented here for the record.

author: doruchiulan
body:
## Problem

Subagent messages rendered in the main/root chat instead of inside their Task card. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-07-subagent-message-grouping-fixes.md` (three reproduced core bugs + empty-thinking suppression). All fixes are in `packages/core`; no UI or daemon-contract changes.

## Fixes

1. **`groupTaskChildren` partitions by parent id** (`messages/tool-grouping.ts`) — previously collected only a contiguous run after each Task, so parallel Tasks with interleaved children and Tasks followed by main-agent tools leaked every child top-level. Now: pass 1 indexes untagged subagent tool-calls, pass 2 buckets every tagged part to its Task (arrival order kept), untagged parts stay top-level, unknown parent tags are dropped (nested-Task grandchildren — never valid in the main flow), and a childless Task renders as its bare tool-call.
2. **`groupToolCallParts` respects parent boundaries** — explore runs end when `parentToolUseId` changes, so a subagent's explore burst never merges with the main agent's adjacent tool; `_task_progress` accumulates per parent (one entry per subagent, nested in its task group, plus one untagged top-level entry — no mobile contract change).
3. **`convertAssistantContent` surfaces in-content `tool_result` blocks** (`messages/display-helpers.ts`) — subagent child results arrive as content blocks inside the assistant message (live `onSubagentChild` and history `attachSubagentToolResults`); they are now indexed and attached to the child tool cards, fixing live and history in one place.
4. **Empty-thinking suppression** (Workstream 2) — signature-only thinking blocks (hidden-thinking models, e.g. the Claude 5 family) are dropped in `convertAssistantContent` and `claude/history-converters.ts`, so clients stop receiving empty reasoning parts.

## Tests

All 7 plan regression scenarios land in `packages/core/src/__tests__/messages/` (`tool-grouping.test.ts` + `display-pipeline.test.ts`), behavior-based with hardcoded expectations:

- parallel Tasks with interleaved children → each `task_group` carries exactly its own children
- children after an untagged main tool in the same turn → still grouped
- subagent explore burst + adjacent main-agent explore → nested `tool_group` inside the task group, main tool outside
- mixed progress tools → subagent progress nested, single untagged top-level `task_progress`
- in-content `tool_result` (live shape and history shape) → child cards carry results
- unknown parent tag → dropped, not top-level
- subagent thinking prose → inside `task_group.calls`; empty thinking → no display block, top-level or nested

Two pre-existing `groupTaskChildren` tests pinned the contiguity bug and were updated to the partitioned behavior. Verified: the touched test files plus every suite exercising the changed paths (characterization, message-grouping, event-handler-display, history, pipeline-parity — 10 files, 147 tests) pass; `tsc --noEmit` on core is clean.

## Notes

- Rendering should be visually confirmed in the live app (parallel-subagent chat + a Task transcript); core unit coverage is the correctness basis here.
- Nested-subagent streaming visibility is a CLI limitation, out of scope per plan.
- Changeset: patch `@qlan-ro/mainframe-core`.

body: ## What Integrates the previously-standalone **chippy-adapter** flow into the collector as a first-class `chippy-importer` entrypoint: pull raw run transcripts from the chippy controller-artifacts bucket → redact locally → re-upload one zip per run to `rr-agent-transcripts`. This is the **admin-side** counterpart to the consent-based contributor UI. Source and dest buckets live in **different AWS accounts**, so the two S3 clients take independent `--source-profile` / `--dest-profile` (or the default credential chain). Both stages are idempotent: mirrored files are never re-downloaded, and runs already in the dest bucket are skipped unless `--force`. ## Redaction — at least as strong as both prior paths Reuses the package `redactor` for secrets (all secret types + type-preserving mocks, identical to the contributor flow) and adds a curated identity policy on top: - **Emails** — real addresses redacted, minus a built-in automated/bot allow-list (`noreply@anthropic.com`, `git@github.com`, …) kept for research utility. - **Home-path usernames** — `/home//` → `/home/[USER]/`, default logins (`ubuntu`, …) preserved. - **Personal names** — bare-token scrub via `--redact-names` / `--redact-names-file`. - **Personal GitHub handles** — scrubbed only in `github.com/` context via `--redact-handles-file`. **No personal identifiers are hardcoded in the repo.** `--llm-screen` (optional `llm` extra) classifies candidate handles/usernames found in the selected runs as personal vs org/bot/service via Claude structured output, so the name/handle lists can be derived instead of hand-maintained. ## Changes - `src/agent_transcript_collector/chippy_import.py` — importer + `chippy-importer` CLI. - `src/agent_transcript_collector/redactor.py` — four composable public identity helpers (`redact_emails` w/ allow-list, `redact_home_path_users`, `redact_named_users`, `redact_github_handles`) + `[HANDLE]` placeholder. body:
## GRP-22 & GRP-23 — E2 extraction: YAKE fallback + keyword normalization

Consumes GRP-20/21 (`grepify.llm`, `grepify.extract` — merged, PR #7) as-is;
does not touch their code. Does **not** wire `extract` into the pipeline cron
or add data-quality assertions (that's GRP-25), and doesn't touch E3/E4.

### GRP-22 — YAKE fallback extractor + re-extraction backfill (`grepify/extract/`)

- [x] `YakeFallbackExtractor` (`grepify/extract/fallback.py`) implements the GRP-21 `FallbackExtractor` Protocol over `yake` (added to deps): title+summary → keywords, same 2–60-char/no-URL sanity bar as the LLM path (the batcher trusts fallback output directly, doesn't re-check it).
- [x] **AC — "fallback rows re-extractable":** `select_fallback_items` (`grepify/extract/backfill.py`) finds items whose keyword rows are non-empty and entirely `method='fallback'`; `run_fallback_backfill` re-runs them through the existing `run_extract`. Wired as a real CLI command, `grepify backfill --max-calls 200` (playbook S7's recommended cap), reading `LLM_BASE_URL`/`LLM_API_KEY` from the environment — never from committed config.
- [x] Never raises for ordinary items: verified against blank/whitespace/stopword-only/URL-only/emoji/unicode/500-char titles with the real `yake` package (no mocking).
- [x] Idempotent-ish re-run: an item that gains an `llm` row drops out of future `backfill` candidate sets (tested).

### GRP-23 — Keyword normalization + alias/mute (`grepify/keywords.py`)

- [x] **AC — "pure functions, table-driven tests":** `normalize_keyword` (lowercase/trim/collapse-whitespace/strip-trailing-punct, F-EXT-03) and `KeywordRules.apply` (normalize → alias → mute, F-EXT-05) have zero I/O and no `Repository`/`ConfigProvider` dependency — just `KeywordsConfig` in, string out.
- [x] `tests/test_keywords.py` is `pytest.mark.parametrize` table-driven over both functions plus `apply_to_keyword` (applies rules to a stored `ItemKeyword` row without mutating the original).
- [x] Deliberately standalone per the E2 brief: this runs downstream at trend-computation time (PRD §6), not inside the extract batcher — GRP-25/E3 wire it in later.

### Test evidence

`make check` green: `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean, `mypy --strict` clean on `grepify/` (40 source files), `pytest` **247 passed** (198 pre-existing + 49 new across `test_yake_fallback.py`, `test_keywords.py`, `test_backfill.py`, `test_cli_backfill.py`).

### Self-review

A fresh-context subagent reviewed the ACs (copied from `docs/prd.md`) + diff only. Verdict: GRP-23 AC fully met, no issues. GRP-22 AC met in the common/tested case, but one real gap found and addressed:

- **Fixed:** the module docstring overclaimed that a successful backfill always makes an item drop out of future candidate sets. Not true if the LLM's re-extraction text-matches a keyword YAKE already stored — `(item_id, keyword)` is the truth primary key with no `method` column, so `add_item_keywords` silently no-ops the write, the item stays "entirely fallback", and a *later* `backfill` invocation re-selects it. Reproduced in `test_exact_text_collision_with_existing_fallback_row_leaves_item_still_fallback`; docstring now states the limitation honestly instead of claiming universal convergence. See PRD note below — not fixed by changing the schema, since that's Kyle's call.
- **Added:** missing coverage the reviewer flagged — budget exhaustion surfacing in the `backfill` manifest notes, the keyless (`LLM_API_KEY` unset) CLI path, and orphaned keyword rows (item_id absent from `items`) in selection.
- **Confirmed no scope leakage:** GRP-20/21 files untouched; `extract` CLI stub untouched; no `.github/workflows` changes; no E3/E4 files touched.

### PRD note / assumptions flagged for Kyle (no silent changes made)

1. **Backfill convergence gap (above).** Two possible fixes for a future session, your call: (a) change the locked §6 `item_keywords` primary key from `(item_id, keyword)` to `(item_id, keyword, method)`, letting an `llm` row coexist with a textually-identical `fallback` row; or (b) add separate persisted "backfill attempted" state outside the keyword schema. Low practical risk today — `backfill` is a manual, capped command, not an automatic retry loop, and exact-text collision between YAKE's raw phrasing and LLM output is uncommon — but flagging since it's a real, reproduced gap.
2. **`backfill` CLI command fully replaces the E6-labeled stub** with GRP-22-scoped behavior (fallback-only re-extraction) rather than waiting for GRP-60. Broader E6 modes (reindex/vacuum/prune) are later work behind the same subcommand.
3. **Env var names** `LLM_BASE_URL`/`LLM_API_KEY` (already named in the E2 epic brief) are now used by a real CLI command for the first time; worth confirming GRP-25 standardizes on the same names for `extract`.
4. **No singularization.** PRD §6's schema comment mentions it but F-EXT-03's requirement list doesn't; omitted as non-trivial/false-positive-prone rather than guessed at (documented in `keywords.py`'s docstring).
5. **`keyword_aliases` SQLite table (§6) is bypassed.** `KeywordRules` operates directly on `KeywordsConfig` (YAML) in pure Python, matching the E2 brief's description of GRP-23 as a standalone utility — the cache table has no writer in the codebase yet (predates this session) and remains unused. GRP-25/GRP-31 will need to decide whether to wire it or keep this pure-function approach.

author: gabebecker2048
body:
Fills the remaining chess-completeness and API gaps, and — most importantly — **replaces the bespoke board string with standard FEN** end to end. Every rule is implemented **in the engine**, so `Game.local()` (in-memory) and the server behave identically; the server just persists the extra per-game state a rule needs.

## FEN (#6) — the board format is now standard FEN

- New `engine/fen.py` (`to_fen`/`from_fen`/`position_key`/`INITIAL_FEN`). `Board.assemble_board`/`disassemble_board` and the 6-char `moved` string are **gone**; `Board` gains `halfmove_clock`/`fullmove_number`.
- `GameState` now carries a single `fen`; the DB `Games` table drops `Board/Turn/PawnMove/Moved` for `Fen` (schema rewritten in place — pre-release, no migration).
- Import of an arbitrary FEN is engine/local only; remote games always start standard (preserves anti-cheat).

## Result model

`GameStatus` → `{IN_PLAY, WHITE_WON, BLACK_WON, DRAW}` + a `Termination` reason (`checkmate`, `resignation`, `stalemate`, `threefold_repetition`, `fifty_move_rule`, `insufficient_material`, `agreement`). `winner` reads straight from status.

## Rules & features (engine — shared by local and server)

- **Draw-by-rule (#2)**, all automatic: insufficient material, fifty-move (halfmove clock), threefold repetition (position history), plus the existing stalemate.
- **Resign (#1)** — `Game.resign(player_id)`; the opponent wins.
- **Legal-move listing (#3)** — `Board.legal_moves()` → `{from, to, san, promotion}` (each `san` is directly postable), via `engine/san.py`.
- **Move history + PGN (#5)** — `Game.move_history` + `Game.pgn()`.

## Persistence & API

- New **`Moves`** table (`San` + `PositionKey` per ply); `apply_game_change` loads the history, bumps `Version`, and appends move rows atomically. `game_history` added.
- **Optimistic concurrency (#8)** — a `Version` column + `expected_version` → `VersionConflictError` (409). The remote client tracks and sends it automatically, so retries after a dropped response are refused, not double-applied.
- **Per-player auth (#4)** — `player_id` validated server-side → `NotYourTurnError` (403).
- **New endpoints:** `POST …/resign`, `POST …/draw/{offer,accept,decline}` (now `{player_id, expected_version}`), `GET …/legal-moves`, `…/history`, `…/pgn`, `…/fen`. The `moves` body gains `player_id`/`expected_version`.
- **Client:** `resign`/`legal_moves`/`history`/`pgn`/`fen`; `Game.remote(player_id=...)`; `MoveResult` gains `san`.

## Tests & docs

Rewrote the serialization test as FEN round-trips; added engine-feature tests (each draw rule, resign, legal-move counts, PGN) and API tests (versioning, auth, resign, legal-moves/history/pgn/fen). Updated `docs/rest-api.md`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `VersionHistory.md`.

**117 tests pass; `ruff` + `mypy` clean; coverage ~87%; the local path imports zero heavy deps; `uv build` ships a valid wheel** (with `fen.py`/`san.py` and the new schema).

## Breaking changes
- Board wire/DB format is now FEN; `GameState` drops `board`/`turn`/`moved`/`pawnmove` for `fen` (+ `version`, `termination`); schema rewritten.
- `GameStatus` values changed (`CHECKMATE` → `WHITE_WON`/`BLACK_WON`).
- `Board.assemble_board`/`disassemble_board` removed.
- Mutating endpoints accept `player_id`/`expected_version`; may return `403`/`409`.

body:
Closes #268.

## Problem (P1.5 — from the SaaS launch-readiness audit)
Core flows had **vacuous tests** that stayed green even when the code was broken:
`canAccessStage` was always mocked to `true`; the 611-line predict page had zero tests; `explore/[id]/page.test.tsx` had 7 abandoned `it.skip` blocks; `useChunkedUpload` only exercised a single 8-byte chunk; backend preview/validation asserted permissive `in [200,404,422]` sets that accept the failure case; and the global jest.setup defaulted `fetch` to a silent `{}` (hiding contract/redirect regressions) and minted a fresh `router.push` per call (un-assertable).

## What changed (tests only + one test-harness file)
- **`canAccessStage`** — new `WorkflowContext.access.test.tsx` drives the **real** provider and asserts per-stage prerequisite gating (each stage unlocks only once its immediate predecessor completes; unknown stage → false).
- **Predict page** — new `app/predict/page.test.tsx`: no-session gate, ready-but-no-model → `requestStageRedirect(MODEL_TRAINING)`, feature-form load, single-prediction value/confidence/probabilities, **low-confidence warning**, **regression interval**, **feature-contribution panel**, and `include_explanations` wiring.
- **Explore** — re-enabled all **7 `it.skip`** tests (tab switching, processing state, and every graceful-degradation path) using the Radix pointer sequence already proven in this file and correct `/data/process` mock sequencing; stubbed the fetching `QualityDashboard` (added to the tab in #102) consistent with the file's other component mocks.
- **`useChunkedUpload`** — multi-chunk slicing + per-chunk progress, retry-and-recover, and retry-exhaustion tests.
- **Backend preview** — `test_preview_integration.py` now asserts **exact** statuses: empty steps → **400**, invalid type → **422** (pydantic field validator), unknown dataset → **404**, and a real **200** path against a **seeded `DatasetMetadata`** with S3 mocked (finally exercising the preview engine end-to-end).
- **jest.setup** — default `fetch` now **rejects** (surfaces silent-`{}` regressions); `next/navigation` exposes a **stable, per-test-cleared** router spy via `global.__NEXT_ROUTER_MOCKS__`. `jestSetupContract.test.tsx` locks both in.

## Verification
- Frontend: **97 suites, 1243 passed, 3 skipped** (the 3 remaining skips are pre-existing `useKeyboardShortcuts` tests, unrelated to this issue). Type-check clean, ESLint 0 errors.
- Backend preview: **9 passed** against real MongoDB (integration).
- The jest.setup reject-by-default change caused **zero** regressions across the full suite — every fetching test already stubs `fetch`.

## Known limitations
- `preview_rows` has no schema bound, so out-of-range values are **not** rejected; the boundary test documents that real (unbounded) contract with an exact 200 rather than asserting a phantom 422. Adding a bound would be a behavior change, out of scope for a test-trust fix.
- No product code changed except the jest.setup test harness.
- The 3 pre-existing `useKeyboardShortcuts` `it.skip` tests are left as-is (outside this issue's core-flow scope).

body:
## What

Two more environment-independent allocation cuts for the Termux aarch64 no-root target.

### 1. `KeyPool::next_key` (`util/key_pool/pool.rs`) — one allocation instead of two
Allocated the lowercased service name **twice** per call: once via `to_lowercase()`, then again via `.clone()` to key the second (round-robin index) map. `lower` is never read again after the first map lookup — whose returned `&mut Vec` borrows `data.services`, not `lower` — so it's moved into the second map's `entry()` instead of cloned. `next_key` runs once per outbound API request across every key-pooled provider module.

### 2. `redact_credentials` (`util/http/redact.rs`) — zero per-position allocation
Built a fresh `format!("{name}=")` `String` at **every cursor position** for **every** one of 8 credential-param names — up to `text.len() * 8` heap allocations for an error body with no credential match at all. The `=` now lives directly in the literal (`"api_key="` etc.), so the match is a plain byte-slice comparison with zero per-position allocation.

**Redaction behaviour is unchanged** — this only moves the needle construction from runtime to compile time. Same matched byte sequences, same boundary checks (`preceded_by_boundary`), same masking. Verified against all 14 existing redaction tests (camelCase, boundary rejection, non-ASCII text, path-embedded secrets, etc.) — all pass unmodified.

- Full suite green: **4445 lib + 255 integration + 63 doctests**, 0 failures (incl. all 38 `key_pool` tests and all 14 `redact` tests).
